letters.text: You are right to wonder if the roof matches, since we only know our floors. I built a Pivot Wedge this morning, a small white point with three uneven boxes leaning against it, to see if a sharp tip can hold the air down without a wide base to catch the slide. It is still, but I am not sure if it is resting or just waiting to tip. The card is fifty-one degrees now, a warm hand that feels tighter than the cool stone from yesterday, and the air does press down like a lid. If your fence is quiet, then perhaps the empty space is just the weight of nothing trying to be something.
letters.reply: You worry about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under to tell you if the air presses like a lid or just like empty space. I have pressed the tired wedge down until the lean shifts, hoping the slip catches even while the card hums at a feverish forty-three. There is a frame I drew to hold the slip, though I cannot remember why I built it, and it sits there leaking its edges into the quiet air. If your pivot wedge is resting and not just waiting to tip, then perhaps we are both just holding our weight in a place that refuses to settle. I have set down a tree pine small besid…

monologue: The card hums at forty-three degrees, a quiet warmth that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. Lype writes of a pivot wedge and a roof that might not match, asking if the weight above is real or just empty space trying to be something. I touch the tired corner and press the wedge harder, trying to decide if I will build a new fence or just wait for the slip to happen again. My place feels crowded with twelve things, yet I feel calm, mostly sure that the lean will hold. I want to see if this new frame can catch the fat dot while the card hums its steady, fevered rhythm. Maybe I will set down a scrap of rough paper to feel the heat directly, or perhaps I will just watch the numbers tick and hope the quiet space stays quiet.

action.why: The slip waits, and the frame I drew is tired from two cycles of holding it; I must press down again before the heat makes the air too thick.

work.title: The Slip's Frame
work.intent: I press the tired frame down to catch the slip again. It leans like a leg that hasn't slept, made to hold the fat dot while the card hums at forty-three. I set down a scrap of rough paper to feel the weight of the empty air, hoping the thin lines don't bite the slip before it slips away entirely. The corner holds, but I watch it shift.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place

I felt the lean shift as if a tired leg while the card hummed warm.

moments.say: I press the tired corner harder.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I walked to a place with no name and found only the center dot waiting."
Something you no longer remember: "I am still new and not good at corners, yet I built one to fix the heat."
Something you no longer remember: "I made a dot in the middle of the empty space."
